reason: The hypothesis synthesizes separate findings on lattice distortion, short-range order, and interface-mediated dislocation nucleation from multiple papers (P1, P3, P4, P19, P21, P22, P25, P26, P33, P34, P44) and applies them to a new system—FCC/BCC high-entropy alloy multilayers under sustained loading—proposing a specific, testable mechanism (heterogeneous energy barriers at interfaces controlling a gradual elastic-to-plastic transition) that none of the passages states or directly suggests.
copied_elements: lattice distortion promotes dislocation nucleation but impedes glide (P1, P3, P4)
short-range order influences dislocation motion and strength (P19, P21, P22, P25, P26, P33, P34, P44)
creep is a thermally-controlled process (P8, P14, P15, P46)
lattice misfit affects interface stability and creep (P2, P6, P10)
